t: You're at the site of St Benet Fink, on what is now Threadneedle Street. The church is gone, but it has a long history. It was recorded from the 13th century, destroyed in the Great Fire of London in 1666, and then rebuilt to designs by Sir Christopher Wren. He was given responsibility for rebuilding fifty-two City churches after the fire, and he is best known for St Paul's Cathedral, completed in 1710. Wren's church here was demolished between 1841 and 1846, so it served the parish for around two centuries after the fire.
